terms.gloss: an underground passage, a tunnel under a road or hill
evidence: Sen. Ep. 57.1: the crypta Neāpolītāna, the road tunnel from Naples to Puteoli (Lewis & Short s.v. crypta)
terms.comment: A covered or underground passage (Lewis & Short: “a concealed, subterranean passage”); Seneca’s is a road through a hill.

evidence: M-O s.v. viaduct: viae ductus, after Egger
terms.comment: Traupman gives it for “underpass”, but the word is the modern Latin for a viaduct, a road carried over something (Morgan–Owens), not under it. Not in Lewis & Short.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 400.
